newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suez Canal freezes transit tolls for third year.
newsitem.headline: Suez Canal freezes transit tolls for third year.

text.p: The Suez Canal Authority (SCA), facing a continue decline in revenues, decided to keep transit tolls unchanged for 1997, the third year in a row, an SCA economic unit official said on Friday.
"The calendar year 1997 will be the third year... without any increases," the official told Reuters.
The official expected that the SCA would even offer new discounts as incentives in a bid to overcome the problem of falling traffic volume and revenues.
The SCA has recently offered a series of discounts to various types of ships.
Toll cuts could be given for container ships, grain bulk carriers and tankers carrying LNG from the Gulf to Europe, the official added.
The canal is facing stiff competition from the SUMED pipeline which pumps crude from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean and from the Cape route around Africa's southern tip.
